title: The Word That Arrived from Another Text
title_ja: 別の文章から届いた言葉
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。架空の事例・論説。実在の企業、作品、調査、実証結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A reader encountering a phrase in a piece of writing may recognize its literal meaning without recognizing that the phrase resembles something encountered in another work.
sentences.ja: ある文章で表現に出会った読者は、その文字通りの意味を認識しても別作品で出会ったものに似ていると気づかないことがある。

sentences.en: For a reader familiar with the earlier work, however, the expression may create an association that affects the interpretation of the passage in which it appears.
sentences.ja: しかし以前の作品に詳しい読者には、その表現が出現箇所の解釈に影響する連想を生む場合がある。

sentences.en: The significance of a phrase can consequently depend partly on its relationship to language beyond the immediate text, although that relationship may not be equally apparent to every reader.
sentences.ja: そこで表現の意義は直近本文を超えた言語との関係にも依存し得るが全読者に等しく明白とは限らない。

sentences.en: An invented example illustrates how such a relationship might enrich a reading without making every other interpretation invalid.
sentences.ja: 創作例はその関係が他の全解釈を無効にせず読みを豊かにする方法を例示する。

sentences.en: Imagine a story about a child who returns to a town after spending several years in another part of the country.
sentences.ja: 国内の別地域で数年過ごした後、町に戻る子供についての物語を想像しよう。

sentences.en: Near the end of the story, the character describes the streets as familiar but notices that a number of activities that once shaped daily life no longer take place there.
sentences.ja: 物語の終盤、人物は通りを身近と描写するがかつて日常を形作った活動のいくつかがもはや行われないと気づく。

sentences.en: The character uses an expression that also appeared in a fictional poem describing a person's inability to return to an earlier moment in life.
sentences.ja: 人物は人生の以前の時点に戻れないことを描写する架空詩にも出た表現を使う。

sentences.en: A reader who has not encountered the poem might interpret the words as a description of the child's immediate disappointment, while a reader familiar with it might notice a broader connection involving the passage of time.
sentences.ja: 詩を知らない読者は言葉を子供の目の前の失望の描写と解釈するが、詩に詳しい読者は時間経過を含むより広いつながりに気づくかもしれない。

sentences.en: Both readings can draw on the events described in the story, but the second has been informed by an additional literary association.
sentences.ja: 両方の読みが物語の出来事に根拠を置けるが、第二の読みには追加の文学的連想が影響している。

sentences.en: A teacher presenting the invented story asks students to consider whether knowing the earlier poem changes the way they understand the child's experience.
sentences.ja: 創作物語を提示する教師は以前の詩を知ることが子供の経験の理解方法を変えるか考えさせる。

sentences.en: Some students recognize a connection between the character's disappointment and the impossibility of recovering a former version of everyday life.
sentences.ja: 何人かは人物の失望とかつての日常生活を回復できないことのつながりを認識する。

sentences.en: Others point out that the new interpretation does not make the specific changes experienced by the child any less important to the story.
sentences.ja: 別の生徒は新解釈が子供の経験した具体的変化を物語にとって重要でなくするわけではないと指摘する。

sentences.en: The discussion consequently distinguishes the information that an additional text can provide from the aspects of the original work that must still be examined independently.
sentences.ja: そこで議論は追加本文が提供できる情報と元作品でなお独立して調べるべき側面を区別する。

sentences.en: Students are encouraged to explain how their revised reading is supported by details from the story rather than merely announcing that they recognize a reference.
sentences.ja: 生徒は単に参照に気づいたと告げるのでなく修正解釈が物語の細部にどう支持されるか説明するよう促される。

sentences.en: The teacher also asks whether a resemblance between expressions necessarily establishes that one author deliberately referred to another work.
sentences.ja: 教師は表現の類似が一作者が意図的に別作品を参照したことを必ずしも確定するかも尋ねる。

sentences.en: Two pieces of writing might contain similar wording for reasons unrelated to a specific intention to establish a connection between them.
sentences.ja: 二文章が両者間につながりを確立する特定意図と無関係な理由で似た言い回しを含むこともある。

sentences.en: A reader can discuss the effects of an association without claiming to have established the circumstances in which the words were originally selected by a real author.
sentences.ja: 読者は実在作者が当初言葉を選んだ事情を確定したと主張せず連想の効果を議論できる。

sentences.en: The fictional exercise therefore separates a question about the interpretation of language from a question about the historical evidence required to establish an author's intention.
sentences.ja: そこで架空活動は言語解釈の問いと作者の意図を確定するため必要な歴史的証拠の問いを区別する。

sentences.en: Literary understanding may develop through the recognition of connections between works as well as through close attention to the language of an individual text.
sentences.ja: 文学理解は個別本文の言語への細かな注意だけでなく作品間のつながりの認識を通じ発展し得る。

sentences.en: Those connections create possibilities for interpretation, but they do not automatically determine which claims about the text or its author are justified.
sentences.ja: つながりは解釈の可能性を作るが本文や作者についてのどの主張が正当かを自動的に決定しない。

sentences.en: A phrase that arrives from another text can invite a reader to notice meanings that had previously remained less apparent.
sentences.ja: 別本文から届く表現は以前は目立たなかった意味に気づくよう読者を促すことがある。

sentences.en: Its value lies in the further questions it makes possible rather than in the replacement of careful reading with a single recognizable reference.
sentences.ja: その価値は注意深い読解を一つの認識可能な参照で置き換えるのでなく、可能にするさらなる問いにある。

questions.prompt: Why can readers interpret a familiar phrase differently?
options: Every reader receives a different literal text.
The phrase loses all meaning when its source is unknown.
Literary reading requires identical experiences.
They may bring different knowledge of related works to their reading.
questions.explanation_ja: 関連作品の知識の違い。

questions.prompt: What does the author say about a phrase's significance?
options: It is always fully determined by a dictionary.
It may depend partly on language outside the immediate passage.
It is necessarily obvious to every reader.
It is limited to the grammatical form.
questions.explanation_ja: 本文外の言語との関連。

questions.prompt: What has the fictional child experienced?
options: Returning to a town after years elsewhere.
Writing the earlier poem.
Leaving the town for the first time.
Reading the story aloud in a classroom.

questions.prompt: What wider idea might the earlier poem suggest?
options: The exact location of every street.
The child's ability to change the past.
The impossibility of returning to a former time.
The need to reject the story's literal events.
questions.explanation_ja: 以前の時間に戻れないこと。

questions.prompt: Why do students examine details from the story after recognizing the connection?
options: A recognized reference makes all evidence irrelevant.
The additional association must be related to the original text.
Every association automatically proves the intended meaning.
Students must reject their earlier understanding entirely.
questions.explanation_ja: 元本文の根拠との関連。

questions.prompt: What distinction does the discussion introduce?
options: Fictional events versus the student attendance list.
The language of the poem versus its publication price.
The length of the story versus the length of the lesson.
Information from the additional text versus details of the story itself.

questions.prompt: Why might similar wording not prove intentional reference?
options: All authors always choose words independently.
Readers are forbidden to compare expressions.
Resemblance can arise for reasons other than deliberate reference.
A poem cannot contain words used elsewhere.
questions.explanation_ja: 別の理由で似る可能性。

options: How language can be interpreted and what evidence establishes authorial intention.
When a child moved and when a teacher began work.
Whether poetry is longer than prose and whether either is useful.
How many people read a text and what it costs.
questions.explanation_ja: 解釈と作者意図の歴史的証拠。

options: Known by every reader.
Expressed in a shorter form.
Written in exactly the same words.
Supported by sufficient reasons or evidence.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: Recognizing a reference establishes the author's intentions conclusively.
Literary works cannot be understood without identifying every reference.
Connections between texts may enrich interpretation, but careful reading and evidence still matter.
The literal details of a story should always be ignored.
questions.explanation_ja: 作品間のつながりと根拠。
